title: Seismic Interpretation Copilot
summary: Decompose seismic imagery, extract structured observations, and prepare an evidence-linked interpretation for expert review.
problem: Geoscientists spend substantial time locating chart regions, transcribing metadata, and reconciling visual findings before interpretation can begin.
demoPrompts: Where should human review remain mandatory?
Explain the evidence chain in this workflow.

title: Maintenance Triage Assistant
summary: Combine machine alerts, maintenance history, and technician notes to prioritize inspections and suggest the next diagnostic step.
problem: Maintenance teams receive fragmented alerts and free-text notes, making it difficult to distinguish urgent failures from routine noise.
demoPrompts: Why is this decision support rather than autonomous maintenance?
What data quality checks are needed?

title: KYC Review Workbench
summary: Extract onboarding evidence, flag missing or inconsistent fields, and prepare a review packet for a compliance analyst.
problem: Analysts manually reconcile identity documents, forms, and policy requirements across high-volume onboarding queues.
demoPrompts: Which steps require deterministic rules?
How should the system expose uncertainty?

title: Card Transaction Fraud Detection
summary: Score held-out card transactions with a deployed random forest, apply a fixed review cutoff, and compare model decisions with known outcomes.
problem: Fraud teams must find most fraudulent purchases within a limited review budget without treating a model score as proof.
demoPrompts: Why is the model score not proof of fraud?
How does a 3% review budget determine the cutoff?

title: Pediatric Chest X-ray Prioritization
summary: Score packaged pediatric chest X-rays, apply a validation-selected review policy, and preserve radiologist and clinician authority.
problem: Imaging queues need a reproducible way to test whether an image model could prioritize review without presenting its score as diagnosis or clearance.
demoPrompts: Why is standard review not clearance?
Why must the threshold be selected before touching the test split?

title: Referral-to-Appointment Coordination
summary: Coordinate one referral from submitted documents through specialty routing, authorization, scheduling, patient communication, and accountable escalation.
problem: Referral teams reconcile variable documents, routing requirements, authorization status, appointment capacity, and patient responses across multiple operational handoffs.
demoPrompts: Which referral decisions should use rules instead of AI?
Where must urgency remain a human decision?

title: Online Order Decisions
summary: Follow one online order from Buy Now to the doorstep, expose six business decisions, and design only the AI-relevant work.
problem: The documented fulfilment path hides payment review, oversold inventory, delivery exceptions, support rework, and the different decisions embedded in one order.
outcomes: Payment screening designed through Data, Method, Metric, and Human
demoPrompts: Which of the six decisions should not use AI?
Walk payment screening through Data, Method, Metric, and Human.

title: Assortment Planning Copilot
summary: Explain demand signals, compare assortment scenarios, and draft a planning rationale for a merchant to adjust.
problem: Merchants must combine forecasts, inventory, promotions, and local knowledge when selecting assortments across many locations.
demoPrompts: What belongs in the scenario engine rather than the model?
How can a merchant challenge a recommendation?

title: Resident Service Intake Assistant
summary: Classify a resident request, retrieve the relevant service guidance, and prepare a routed case for staff review.
problem: Residents describe needs in natural language while agencies organize services by program, eligibility, and jurisdiction.
demoPrompts: Why should eligibility remain deterministic?
How should language accessibility be tested?

title: Student Success Planning Assistant
summary: Explain approved academic-success indicators and help an advisor prepare outreach options without making automated student decisions.
problem: Advisors need to interpret scattered course, engagement, and support-service signals while avoiding opaque automated decisions.
demoPrompts: What makes this use case high risk?
How do we prevent automated adverse action?

title: Design Package Review Assistant
summary: Extract design requirements and drawing references, then assemble a traceable review checklist for an engineer.
problem: Reviewers manually trace requirements across specifications, drawings, schedules, and revision packages.
demoPrompts: How should citations work across drawings and specifications?
Which checks should remain rule-based?

title: Fleet Routing Decision Workbench
summary: Combine traffic, delivery windows, vehicle constraints, and disruption signals to prepare route options for a fleet dispatcher.
problem: Dispatchers must continually rebalance routes as congestion, weather, vehicle availability, and customer constraints change.
demoPrompts: Which part is prediction and which part is optimization?
What safety constraints must a dispatcher own?

title: Grounded Campaign Content Studio
summary: Generate campaign drafts from an approved brief and source library, then route claims, rights, and brand checks to an editor.
problem: Creative teams need more variations without losing factual grounding, brand consistency, attribution, or intellectual-property controls.
demoPrompts: Where are attribution and IP checks enforced?
Why is fluency not a quality metric?

title: Crop Stress Monitoring Assistant
summary: Combine field observations, weather, and aerial imagery to prioritize areas for agronomist inspection and intervention planning.
problem: Large growing areas make it difficult to identify emerging water, pest, nutrient, or disease stress early enough for targeted action.
demoPrompts: What can imagery suggest but not prove?
Which business and sustainability metrics should be paired?

title: AI-Assisted Provenance Review
summary: Use an immutable event trail to detect unusual provenance patterns, then prepare evidence for a reviewer without treating blockchain entries as proof of physical truth.
problem: Supply-chain teams can record custody events but still need to detect inconsistencies, missing attestations, and suspicious movement patterns.
demoPrompts: What does an immutable ledger fail to prove?
Why should anomaly detection not trigger an automatic accusation?

title: Credit Risk Early-Intervention Review
summary: Score monthly account snapshots for missed-payment risk, size the review queue with an expected-cost rule, and hand ranked accounts to analysts with plain-language reason codes.
problem: A small credit-risk team can review only a fraction of 30,000 accounts each month, and any adverse step must come with specific reasons the customer can understand.
outcomes: A review queue sized by expected cost
Reason codes behind every flagged account
demoPrompts: Why is this a review queue and not a credit decision?
How does the expected-cost rule size the monthly queue?

title: Customer Complaint Routing Desk
summary: Read each complaint narrative, name the likely specialist team with visible word-level reasons, and auto-route only confident calls while a human triage desk owns the rest.
problem: Banks must answer consumer complaints on a regulatory clock, and a misrouted complaint burns days before the right team even sees it.
outcomes: Fewer misroutes on the response clock
Human triage below the confidence line
demoPrompts: Why route automatically only above a confidence threshold?
What happens when a specialist finds a misrouted complaint?

title: Compressor Health Monitoring and Work Orders
summary: Turn a compressor's sensor stream into six plain-language hourly measures, score how unusual each hour looks, and raise a work order only above a threshold priced against callout and downtime costs.
problem: A depot sees millions of sensor readings and only a handful of documented failures, so a threshold set too low buries technicians in wasted callouts and a threshold set too high lets a unit fail in service.
outcomes: A developing fault caught within hours, not after the breakdown
An alert threshold priced against callout and downtime costs
Technicians who keep the diagnosis and the safety call
patterns: Threshold policy kept outside the model
Scheduled human recalibration as the machine's workload drifts
architecture: One-minute averaging and hourly feature window
demoPrompts: Why does this detect a developing fault rather than forecast one days ahead?
What happens to the alert queue when the machine's normal workload drifts?

title: Maintenance Procedure Lookup Desk
summary: Answer a technician's plain-English question with passages pulled from official safety regulation and equipment manuals, show the citation behind every claim, and say plainly when the answer is not in the documents.
problem: Procedures live across thousands of pages of regulation, site manuals, and equipment books, so technicians answer from memory — and a confident answer citing the wrong rule is a safety failure, not a typo.
outcomes: Every answer carries the rule it came from
A plain refusal when the documents do not cover the question
A qualified person verifies before any work starts
patterns: Refusal as a designed outcome, not an error
The qualified person, never the assistant, authorizes work
architecture: Public-domain regulation, site procedure, and equipment manual corpus
Passage splitter that keeps section labels and citations
Embedding index with a keyword search for comparison
demoPrompts: Why is a refusal the right answer when the rule points at a standard it does not contain?
What breaks when two rulebooks repeat each other almost word for word?

title: Weekly Reorder Planning with Forecast Ranges
summary: Turn a wholesaler's weekly sales history into a demand range for each steady seller, convert that range into an order quantity priced against stockout and overstock costs, and put the quantity in front of a planner who decides.
problem: A single forecast number gives a planner nothing to plan with: order the average and you are short in a good week and sitting on markdown stock in a bad one, and the cost of being short is rarely the same as the cost of being long.
outcomes: A demand range for each steady seller, not a single number
An order quantity that moves when the cost of a stockout changes
A planner who approves, adjusts, or holds every purchase order
capabilities: Weekly demand panel from raw order lines
Point forecast with an empirical prediction interval
patterns: The cost ratio lives in the policy, not in the model
Products with too little history are planned by hand, not forecast badly
The system proposes a quantity and never places an order
architecture: UCI Online Retail II transaction log (CC BY 4.0)
Weekly demand panel builder with cancellations and non-product lines removed
Moving-average point forecast with per-product residual quantiles
Newsvendor order-quantity policy with a configurable cost ratio
Planner approval queue and sell-through log

edges.label: one row per product per week
quantity at the cost-based service level
this week's sales join next week's forecast

demoPrompts: Why does the order quantity change when the cost of a stockout goes from twice to nine times the cost of overstock?
What happens to a Christmas-heavy product when the planner orders at the middle of the range instead of the top?

title: Storefront Recommendation Slots
summary: Fill a fixed number of recommendation slots on a storefront page by ranking products the shopper has not bought before, keeping already-bought items in a separate labeled strip and showing an honest popular-right-now list when there is nothing to personalize on.
problem: A ranking model that scores well offline usually scores well because it is recommending what the shopper already buys, and a model that only ever surfaces the same handful of bestsellers looks accurate while showing a fraction of a percent of the catalog.
outcomes: Recommendation slots judged on products the shopper has never bought
An honestly labeled fallback for shoppers with no usable history
Merchandisers who set the rules the model has to rank inside
capabilities: Customer by product matrix from raw order lines
patterns: Offline ranking scores are reported as ranking scores, never as revenue
A fallback is labeled for what it is instead of dressed up as personalization
Catalog coverage is monitored beside accuracy, not after it
architecture: UCI Online Retail II transaction log (CC BY 4.0)
Customer by product matrix built on a time-based split
Item-item similarity model truncated to the nearest neighbors
Slot eligibility, exclusion, and fallback policy
Slot outcome log and catalog coverage monitor

edges.label: items the shopper has not bought

demoPrompts: Why does the same model finish first on one leaderboard and below random on the other?
What does a high hit rate hide when the model has only ever shown ten products out of thousands?
